mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The mechanism is always active and does not require specific regime conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is positive (IC > 0) in more than 60% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% over 3 months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return is positive when both HOUST and RSAFS decline over the past month in more than 60% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL yoy change > 3.5%), the Federal Reserve typically tightens policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL yoy change > 3.5% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening supply-side activity, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 in absolute value over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when HOUST < 1400 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day SPX return is positive when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises over the past month in more than 60% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 yoy growth > 2.5%), the economy approaches its peak, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to reduced growth momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when GDPC1 yoy growth > 2.5% over a 5-year rolling window.
